findings.current: He and the Roaring Fury Swordsman were the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord’s only two Senior Brothers and the most senior members of the Zhongnan Sect.
findings.defect: The Korean identifies Hwangbo Eom alone as the Zhongnan Sect’s highest-ranking member. The current wording can make both Senior Brothers the most senior members.
findings.rationale: The singular subject 그가 refers to Hwangbo Eom, who is identified as 현 종남파의 최고 배분.
findings.replacement: He and the Roaring Fury Swordsman were the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord’s only two Senior Brothers, and Hwangbo Eom was the highest-ranking member of the Zhongnan Sect.

findings.current: he took Jeok Cheongang’s answer to mean that his Master wanted to give his Disciple the authority to speak.
findings.defect: The translation changes the idea of a Master backing his Disciple into granting the Disciple authority to speak.
findings.rationale: 제자에게 힘을 실어 주기 위한 means to support or back the Disciple, not to give the Disciple authority to speak.
findings.replacement: he took Jeok Cheongang’s answer as a Master’s way of backing his Disciple.

findings.defect: “Curious” can suggest inquisitiveness, but the source describes an odd, inscrutable smile whose meaning is unclear.
findings.rationale: The Korean says 의미를 알 수 없는 묘한 미소, explicitly describing a smile of unclear meaning.

findings.current: he’d cleaned up the messes his Senior Brothers made more than once.
findings.defect: The translation softens the source’s crude image and register.
findings.rationale: 싸질러 놓은 똥 is a deliberately vulgar image, not a neutral reference to messes.
findings.replacement: he’d cleaned up the shit his Senior Brothers had left behind more than once.

summary: The chapter is broadly faithful, but a few passages alter hierarchy, intent, or register.
